Say my shop
makes $10,000.
Why do I
only keep
$3,000?
This is gross
profit.
And this is
net profit.
What's the
difference?
Gross profit is
what's left
after
subtracting the
cost
of making or
buying what you
sell.
Net profit is
what's left
after ALL
business
expenses.
Now,
accounts payable
versus accounts
receivable!
Accounts payable
is money your
business owes.
Accounts
receivable is
money customers
owe your
business.
Remember:
Payable means
you pay.
Receivable means
you receive!
